named_question: Can mood boolean case variants accepted by the native reader be used without normalizing stored spelling or coercing unsupported explicit values?

static_byte_pins.purpose: String comparison uses the case-insensitive imported comparison after explicit null checks; no spelling rewrite.
Boolean reader stores equality with TRUE using that comparator.

source_contract.binding: Move, ReadOnly, SkipNext, MixMod and Sequencing all use the common type0 reader.
source_contract.case: The reader compares case-insensitively with TRUE. ASCII true case variants therefore read true; ASCII false case variants read false.
source_contract.deliberate_subset: Native comparison also produces false for other unequal strings, but CLI does not adopt arbitrary-false coercion. Numeric, whitespace-padded, opaque and non-ASCII lookalike input remains unsupported.
source_contract.preservation: Reading a boolean is not a request to rewrite serialized spelling. A semantically unchanged requested-state edit retains raw spelling and all in-place bytes.

CLI_policy.accepted: ASCII case variants of true/false plus already-recovered omission defaults. Shared parser covers all five read-only flags; only existing guarded SkipNext/MixMod setters are editable.
CLI_policy.no_op: TRUE/tRuE/FALSE/FaLsE are retained exactly when effective value already equals the requested value. Inspection returns raw spelling separately from effective boolean.
CLI_policy.change: A real boolean change writes only the selected requested flag using ordinary lowercase true/false; every unrelated flag's original spelling remains unchanged.
CLI_policy.guards: Keep exact direct selection, SID uniqueness, MixMod role/CID exclusions, missing defaults and all unsupported explicit-value errors. No new raw boolean, permissions or graph-state editor.
